title: Curiosity comes first.
summary: A personal identity for Lay Shah: inventive and discerning, with one unexpected detail that makes a clear impression.

brief.name: Lay Shah
brief.audience: Founders, businesses, and small teams choosing a developer for websites, applications, and practical tools.
brief.direction: Restraint with an unexpected, memorable character.
brief.latitude: Fresh lettering, symbols, and colors are open for exploration. Website typography, colors, and layout are reviewed separately.
brief.ownerWords: At the top, I think it should be curiosity, without which nothing is possible.
brief.interpretation: Explore deeply enough to understand the real need, then explain the choices and value clearly. This is a working creative brief, not a new public tagline.

muse.name: MUBI
muse.alt: Source capture of MUBI’s white wordmark and seven-dot arrangement from its own homepage.
muse.cue: Plain, compact lettering sits beside a small, uneven arrangement of equal-sized dots. The unusual silhouette adds a moment of discovery while the name stays easy to read.
muse.carry: A clear name, an economical shape vocabulary, and one deliberate surprise.
muse.boundary: The dot arrangement, letter shapes, and cinema identity belong to MUBI. Lay’s sketches will explore original forms and ideas.
muse.confirmed: Selected by you: “I would love to go with option C, unexpected character.”

references.name: Josh W. Comeau
references.alt: Source capture of Josh W. Comeau’s colored name, with a tilted W and small caret between the words.
references.observation: A tilted W and a small caret interrupt an otherwise readable name. The surrounding website adds a much more playful illustrated world.
references.lesson: A small, specific change can give lettering a recognizable voice.
references.caution: The whimsical treatment suits his teaching personality. Lay’s clients still need a composed, confident first impression.

references.name: Rauno Freiberg
references.alt: Source capture of Rauno Freiberg’s large black name beside the edge of a yellow circle.
references.observation: The name leads in large, plain lettering. A yellow circle and unusual page composition carry the visual character.
references.lesson: Personality can come from one deliberate interruption around clear typography.
references.caution: This is a name treatment in a larger composition, rather than a standalone graphic symbol. Lay’s finished mark must also hold its own outside the website.

references.name: Paco Coursey
references.alt: Source capture of Paco Coursey’s small, unadorned name on a dark background.
references.observation: A small, unadorned name introduces a restrained, writing-led page. There is no separate graphic logo in this captured heading.
references.lesson: Restraint gives the work and language room to establish credibility.
references.caution: Plain name typography alone offers little visual recognition when removed from its page. Lay needs a more memorable identifying feature.

references.name: Brittany Chiang
references.alt: Source capture of Brittany Chiang’s large pale name and Frontend Engineer label on navy.
references.observation: A large, bold name and a clear role establish an immediate hierarchy against a navy background.
references.lesson: The person’s name can be the clearest anchor in a professional portfolio.
references.caution: Dark backgrounds and neutral sans-serif names recur in this comparison set. Repeating that combination alone would give Lay little distinction.

references.name: Tobias van Schneider / HOVS
references.alt: Source capture of the HOVS serif wordmark in a red tab at the top of Tobias van Schneider’s site.
references.observation: The HOVS wordmark pairs high-contrast serif lettering with an assertive red tab. Tobias’s own products and studio work share the surrounding identity.
references.lesson: A consistent point of view can connect a personal practice and several products.
references.caution: HOVS is a studio identity. Lay Shah remains the primary name here; a new studio name or elaborate badge is outside the brief.

references.name: Bruno Simon
references.alt: Source capture of Bruno Simon’s published square browser icon with a dark diamond and white center.
references.observation: The published browser icon is a simple diamond. The portfolio itself builds recognition through a distinctive interactive driving world.
references.lesson: A logo is one part of a personal identity; demonstrated craft can carry much of its character.
references.caution: An isolated geometric diamond would not give Lay the same distinctive experience. The new mark needs an identifying feature of its own.

findings: Names do much of the identifying work in this set. Josh modifies his lettering; Rauno, Paco, and Brittany largely use their names as typography within a broader composition.
Dark backgrounds and neutral sans-serif lettering recur. They can be well executed, but using them alone would give Lay little visual distinction.
The memorable differences come from particular choices: Josh’s displaced letter, Rauno’s spatial interruption, HOVS’s typographic contrast, and Bruno’s authored experience.
The opportunity for Lay is a composed identity with an identifying detail that survives outside a website. The client should be able to notice that detail before reading its explanation.

criteria.title: Personal relevance
criteria.description: Trace the idea to Lay’s curiosity, understanding, or communication. It should feel plausible for this person and this audience.

criteria.title: Recognizable character
criteria.description: Point to one feature that can be remembered after a brief glance. Keep the name clear and the surprise intentional.

criteria.title: Legibility
criteria.description: Read the name at header size and inspect the compact symbol at actual 16, 24, and 32 pixels. Test pure black and white before color.

criteria.title: Distinction
criteria.description: Compare the visible work against these six identities, MUBI, and the rejected rounds. Record similarities and weaknesses without awarding intent as evidence.

avoid: Reworking the existing LS mark or any of the six rejected concepts.
Copying MUBI’s dots or substituting a familiar tech symbol for a personal idea.
Default curiosity icons such as a magnifying glass, question mark, or eye without a specific original idea.
Using a fashionable font, color effect, or animation as the only source of distinction.
nextStage: Review the reconstructed lettering, symbol proportions and A/B color treatment. After approval, finish the master files and usage guide before applying the identity locally.

concepts.name: Looped name
concepts.idea: A compact lowercase name with a rounded y terminal and a broad descending curve. The y gives your name a detail to recognize.
concepts.risk: The y and the second line sit close together; the join needs refinement at header size.
concepts.alt: Stacked lowercase lay shah, heavy strokes, curled y and circular terminal.
concepts.construction: Raster concept study; no production geometry authored or approved.
concepts.caption: Looped name

concepts.name: Forward name
concepts.idea: The L and S stretch across the two-line name, giving the letters a shared forward movement.
concepts.risk: The speed and sharp terminals could suggest sport or automotive work more than thoughtful consulting.
concepts.alt: Slanted Lay Shah, long angular L and sweeping S, stacked on two lines.
concepts.construction: Raster concept study; no production geometry authored or approved.
concepts.caption: Forward name

concepts.name: Continuous name
concepts.idea: A single-line name with soft joins around ay and a shaped S. It gives the full name priority.
concepts.risk: This is the closest to ordinary typography; the small joins may not make it memorable enough.
concepts.alt: Single-line Lay Shah with rounded sans letterforms and closely connected ay.
concepts.construction: Raster concept study; no production geometry authored or approved.
concepts.caption: Continuous name

concepts.name: Interlocking name
concepts.idea: The curved y and tall S hold the two lines together. Repeated narrow counters make the name feel composed.
concepts.risk: The fine strokes need size testing, and the style may feel closer to fashion or publishing.
concepts.alt: Stacked lay Shah in contrasting thick and thin strokes, with curved y and a terminals.
concepts.construction: Raster concept study; no production geometry authored or approved.
concepts.caption: Interlocking name

concepts.name: Ribbon y
concepts.idea: The y from Lay becomes a small, animated-looking mark. Its branching shape offers a possible connection to asking why.
concepts.risk: The separate circle can read as a person or a bird. The why connection is a word association, not something the shape proves.
concepts.alt: A broad black y with a curved tail and separate round upper-right terminal.
concepts.construction: Raster concept study; no production geometry authored or approved.
concepts.caption: Ribbon y

concepts.name: Split counter
concepts.idea: Two solid pieces frame an interrupted inner shape. This tests whether an abstract initials direction has any appeal.
concepts.risk: The initials are not clear enough. It risks being another arbitrary geometric mark, so I would not lead with it.
concepts.alt: A left semicircular form and a lower curved block separated by white space.
concepts.construction: Raster concept study; no production geometry authored or approved.
concepts.caption: Split counter

concepts.name: Open a
concepts.idea: An open, a-like form uses the letter repeated twice in Lay Shah. Two curved parts face the same central space.
concepts.risk: It can read as a seed or flame before a letter. The connection to your name needs to be visible, not merely explained.
concepts.alt: Two tapered curved forms make a loose lowercase a silhouette with an open central counter.
concepts.construction: Raster concept study; no production geometry authored or approved.
concepts.caption: Open a

concepts.name: Loop y
concepts.idea: A compact y folds its descender into a loop. It is a direct fragment of your first name.
concepts.risk: On its own it may read as a generic script y. The curve needs a more individual construction.
concepts.alt: A black y with two broad branches and a looped descending stroke.
concepts.construction: Raster concept study; no production geometry authored or approved.
concepts.caption: Loop y

concepts.name: Ribbon + name
concepts.idea: Pairs 05 with the lettering from 01 to test a related symbol and name.
concepts.risk: Both y forms compete for attention; the name alone may be stronger.
concepts.alt: Ribbon y to the left of the two-line looped lowercase lay shah.
concepts.construction: Raster concept study; no production geometry authored or approved.
concepts.caption: Ribbon + name

concepts.name: Counter + name
concepts.idea: Pairs 06 with the contrasting strokes of 04 to test a more formal identity.
concepts.risk: The symbol and lettering use different shape languages. The pairing is less convincing than the name alone.
concepts.alt: Split counterform at left beside the tall, high-contrast stacked lay Shah.
concepts.construction: Raster concept study; no production geometry authored or approved.
concepts.caption: Counter + name

concepts.name: Open a + name
concepts.idea: Pairs 07 with a horizontal name, aiming for a compact, readable arrangement.
concepts.risk: The generated symbol has an extra seam and the name is crowded; both need redrawing if this direction appeals.
concepts.alt: An open a-like symbol left of closely spaced single-line Lay Shah, with a small seam in the symbol.
concepts.construction: Raster concept study; no production geometry authored or approved.
concepts.caption: Open a + name

concepts.name: Loop y + name
concepts.idea: Pairs 08 with the slanted name from 02. This tests how much energy the identity should have.
concepts.risk: The repeated y and sweeping capitals make this busy. It may communicate speed more than curiosity.
concepts.alt: Looped y next to angled, two-line Lay Shah with extended L and S strokes.
concepts.construction: Raster concept study; no production geometry authored or approved.
concepts.caption: Loop y + name

sketchGroups.title: 01–04 / The name
sketchGroups.description: Four different structures for Lay Shah. Compare their character and readability.

sketchGroups.title: 05–08 / Letters as symbols
sketchGroups.description: A narrower exploration from your name. Each has limitations; none is presented as a finished solution.

sketchGroups.title: 09–12 / Pairing tests
sketchGroups.description: These reuse the symbols above to test their relationship with lettering. They are four combinations, not four additional symbol ideas.

recommendation.reason: Start by comparing 01 and 04: the first feels more approachable, the second more formal. In this sheet I think the name carries more character than the separate symbols. Neither is selected. If neither feels like you, describe the feature that feels wrong rather than choosing a pair.

rejectionFeedback: The owner rejected the entire previous twelve: lettering felt like font changes, symbols lacked personal relevance, and combinations felt generic.
reviewNote: A fresh black-and-white study of your name and its letter shapes. The previous twelve have been withdrawn. These are AI-assisted image studies for visual feedback; a chosen direction still needs original vector drawing, spacing and small-size testing.

artwork.tool: Built-in image_gen, generation followed by one edit
artwork.alt: Twelve black-and-white Lay Shah studies arranged in three rows. First row: four name treatments with looped, slanted, continuous and high-contrast lettering. Second row: a ribbon y, split counterform, open a-like form and looped y. Third row pairs those symbols with the name. Numbered descriptions follow.

selection.scope: Develop 09 as the full identity and 05 as its compact symbol. One family, not two competing identities. Final treatment and integration remain unapproved.

development.title: The ribbon y, developed.
development.summary: Your selected 05 / 09 family, rebuilt as editable curves. The symbol keeps its detached dot and sweeping tail; the name gets clearer spacing and a quieter y.

treatments.name: A / Evergreen
treatments.note: A deeper green on warm paper. Closest to the existing website, with a softer background.

treatments.name: B / Cobalt
treatments.note: A brighter blue on a cool white. More assertive; this would be a separate palette decision.

critiques: The curved y is recognizable, but the detached dot can still suggest a person or a bird.
The name is reconstructed from the selected sketch, not traced or set in a replacement font. Its letter shapes need your review.
The horizontal application uses the same stacked name beside a smaller symbol. A true single-line name would need separate drawing.
development.recommendation: I recommend A / Evergreen for continuity with the site. Keep the name prominent and use the symbol alone in compact spaces. Color and this reconstructed lettering are proposals for your review.
development.status: Development preview only. No final kit or public branding update.
